payload.text: the login flow breaks on refresh, find out why
The report says the login flow breaks on refresh, so the first suspect is whatever the refresh endpoint does differently from the initial login.
Refresh usually means re-authenticating with a long-lived token, so the cookie handling is the natural place to look: if the session cookie is re-read before the new token is rotated into the store,
the refresh would validate the old token and fail the first time, then succeed on the retry once the rotation has landed. That would look exactly like an intermittent break on refresh only.
Before reading code I should check the auth middleware order: the handler that rotates the token has to run before anything that reads the session back out of the request context.
If they run in the wrong order the old cookie is validated, the rotation is discarded, and the user is bounced to the login page with no error anywhere in the logs.
The session store is internal/auth/session.go by the layout, so that is where RotateToken and ReadSession will live. I will read it first, then the middleware wiring if there is one.
A second possibility is clock skew on the token's issued-at claim, but that would break far more than refresh, so it stays at the bottom of the list.
Plan: read the session store, find the refresh path, check the order of rotate versus validate, write a test that refreshes twice in a row, and only then propose a fix.
Let me read the session store and trace the refresh path.
Confirmed: Refresh calls ReadSession on the incoming cookie before it calls RotateToken, so the old token is validated and only afterwards rotated.
The fix is to rotate first and read the session back from the rotated record, or to validate against the stored record the rotation is about to replace rather than the cookie the client sent.

## What I found

`RotateToken` runs **after** `ReadSession` in `Refresh`, so a refresh validates the old token and bounces the user before the rotation lands.
Swapping the two calls fixes it. Want me to apply the fix?
